summary: The whole-label deficit argument is valid: each deficit is assigned exactly once to a minimizing physical endpoint, the pooled endpoint identity bounds every endpoint charge, and the exact cut count yields the stated strengthened lower bound. The missed-block and reservoir estimates then give the strict H_int bound, and the synchronized rank-five selector inequality applies with the correct mass, rank, and constants to give R_sel(C)>14Q/825>Q/100. All invoked predecessor hypotheses and quantifiers match, including endpoint distinctness, endpoint-disjointness, nonnegative charges, positivity of the selector support, collision aggregation, and the all-loop case.
